page0.text:
"...It's morning."
I slowly open my eyes.
The night that I thought would last forever ended before I realized it.

page1.text:
"...That's good. The pain is gone."
I must've not been able to bear it anymore, or it stopped hurting before I knew it.
Either way, I don't feel any further pain, nor do I feel sleepy or sluggish.
I was able to sleep for about three hours, and my mind is pretty clear.

page2.text:
"All right. I'll go make breakfast."
My bed is wet from sweating.
I force myself up.
And as soon as I try to stand, my left foot slips.

page3.text:
"Huh?"
I try touching my left foot.
There's nothing wrong.
There is no pain or bleeding, but...there's also no sensation at all.

page4.text:
"...Hm."
It's not just my left leg, either. I don't feel anything in my left arm.
I try pinching the left side of my chest and feel nothing there as well.

page5.text:
"..."
Has my body still not healed completely?
The whole left side is numb, and I'm feeling a strange disconnect, like it's someone else's body. Uhh, I have had similar experiences before...

page6.text:
"Like when I sleep in the shed. If I use my arm as a pillow, it'll often feel like this."
Yeah, of course.
This is similar to the numbing that one gets when the blood circulation in their limbs temporarily gets cut off.

page7.text:
Well, I can move it, so I guess it'll go back to normal eventually.
Though my limbs react frustratingly slowly, like I'm moving them by pulling a lever, it hopefully won't affect my daily activity if I'm careful.

page8.text:
I refrain from using a knife this morning and make a simple meal with some bread.
My dominant hand, the right hand, is safe, so I can use a frying pan.
I cook bacon and eggs, prepare instant clam chowder for the three of us, and somehow manage to set up the table.

page9.text:
"Thank you for the meal."
"Dig in."
We both bite into the golden bread.

page10.text:
Saber nods in approval at the toast and salad.
...Yeah.
It's interesting seeing Saber holding a rice bowl and chopsticks, but Western food seems more appropriate.

page11.text:
...
Saber is quiet.
Though she isn't unfriendly, she does consider silence as a virtue.
She's like this especially during meals.
It's more comfortable for me when it's quiet during meals, so a breakfast like this is ideal.

page12.text:
"...Huh?"
I finally realize then why it's so quiet this morning.

page14.text:
"Hey, good morning! ...Wait, huh? Are we having French food this morning?"
Fuji-nee wasn't staying over.

page15.text:
"That's right. I tried my hand at something Café Marly-esque. So please sit and eat."
I hand Fuji-nee her mug.

page16.text:
"Hm? But you know, it smells like instant food, Shirou."
"It's your imagination. Your nose isn't working since you just woke up."

page17.text:
"I see. You might be right. Oh, good morning, Saber. Sorry I couldn't come by last night."
Fuji-nee gulps down hot clam chowder like a sports drink.
She must have some kind of special coating along her esophagus.

page18.text:
"Good morning, Taiga. I did not see you yesterday, but did something happen?"
"Hm? Yeah, I had to work... Well, no. I was just going around visiting those in the hospital. But that ended yesterday, so I can relax again today."

page19.text:
She puts margarine on her toast.
Though it doesn't really matter, Fuji-nee doesn't use butter for some reason.
I'd try asking why, but I feel like I'd get some sort of stupid response. I'll table that for another day.

page20.text:
"...Hey Fuji-nee, how many of the ones hospitalized are in a serious condition?"
"No one's in a serious condition. They're all just staying at the hospital to be safe, and they said that everyone can go back to school next week.
So it's okay, Shirou. Don't worry about this accident. You can go to school without worry."

page21.text:
Fuji-nee bites into her toast with gusto.
I feel reassured just by watching her. She really looks unconcerned.

page22.text:
"...I see. That's good."
"Yes, all's right with the world. I'll be looking forward to dinner tonight."

page23.text:
That peaceful smile.
...Yeah. At times like this, I'm reminded that Fuji-nee is still Fuji-nee.

page24.text:
"I'll get going now. Please take care of the house as usual, Saber."
"Yes, that is fine, but... Shirou, I did not see anything made in the kitchen, so am I to go without lunch today...?"

page25.text: "...Mm? Oh, sorry. We have half days on Saturday. I'll be a bit late, but I'll come back by lunchtime, so I'll make lunch."

page26.text: "I see. Shirou, you must tell me these things beforehand. You do not seem to be on top of things this morning. You have been reacting slowly as well. Is something the matter?"

page27.text:
"Huh? No, not really. My body is still heavy from yesterday, but it should go back to normal soon."
Sensation hasn't returned to the left side of my body yet, but there should be no problem as I can still move it.
I don't need to make Saber worry over something like this.

page28.text:
"Well, you're right that I should tell you. Meals are your only hobby. I'll make a big lunch to make up for it, so let's call it even."
I wave goodbye and go to the door.

page29.text:
"No. I cannot agree with what you just said. It is only that I would not have energy in the case of an emergency if I skip meals—"
"Okay, okay. See you later, Saber!"

page30.text:
I leave Saber's complaints behind me.
"Woah... This is more tiring than I thought."

page31.text:
I touch my numb left foot.
It was fine back home, but now that I'm walking this is starting to make me feel ill.
Even if it doesn't affect my movements, it seems to affect me mentally to walk dragging a body with no senses.

page32.text:
"...No, I can't complain about something like this. The others had it way worse."
Even though she healed, Saber got her throat crushed and was smashed against a wall.
Tohsaka was coughing from receiving that blow from Kuzuki.
Compared to those two, it's nothing since I didn't actually get wounded.

page33.text:
"...Well..."
I force my leg to move and start down the hill.
...I feel slightly nauseous.
With uncertain steps, I make it down the usual path to school, weaving around like a ghost.

page34.text:
And so...
School's over before I knew it.

page35.text:
It might be because my body still doesn't feel right, but my sense of time is all over the place.
I don't remember any of the material from class, and I'm not too sure of what I did either.

page36.text:
"...Could this really be serious?"
The left side of my body doesn't change.
It makes me depressed feeling so numb for this long.

page37.text:
"And the sensation is getting stronger, like everything is heavier."
...My nausea isn't going away. And of course, Kuzuki wasn't at school.

page38.text:
"...I should go home. Saber should be hungry too."
I grab my bag and stand from my seat.
Amidst all this, I feel like I'm forgetting something. Though I figure I'll remember once I get home.

page39.text:
"Oh..."
Once I finish walking up the hill with my numb left foot, I remember what I forgot.

page40.text:
"I forgot to talk to Tohsaka."
So preoccupied was I that it completely slipped my mind. My spacey, hazy mind.
Well, I'm sure nothing important happened since she didn't immediately come find me.
Considering my condition, I can just contact her once I get better.

page41.text:
"I'm home."
I call out in a loud voice so Saber can hear from her room and go straight to the kitchen.

page42.text:
I put the ingredients that I bought in the refrigerator, wash my hands, and put on my apron.
The plan is to make cod for dinner, so for lunch it'll be some kind of meat or poultry.
A meal of chicken teriyaki for the main course sounds good, so I get to work on that.

page43.text:
"Are you home, Shirou?"
Saber must've heard the noise, as she comes in from the porch.

page44.text:
"Yeah, sorry I'm late. I'll make lunch right away, so you can rest. You must be hungry—"
...Crap.
I got distracted by Saber and dropped the plate in my hand.

page45.text:
"Shirou, the plate is broken."
"Yeah. It's my first time breaking a plate."
I'm surprised myself. Surprised enough to say something stupid, too.

page46.text:
"Sorry. I'll clean it up right away, so you can go sit down."
I pick up a piece.
"...Huh?"
I fumble and drop it too.

page47.text:
"...You seem tired, Shirou.
No, I will clean it up. Please focus on cooking."

page48.text:
I guess trying to pick it up with my left hand was a mistake.
...Well, it was a good lesson.
My left hand still hasn't regained feeling. I'll need to be incredibly careful with a knife.

page49.text:
"Shirou. Please do not push yourself. Make something simple. I am happy that you are putting in the effort, but I'd rather not have blood mixed into the meal."
Well, I don't want that either.
That is a failure for someone in charge of the kitchen.

page50.text:
"All right. I'll put effort into dinner and make lunch simple. I'll still make the main dish, but I won't be using any pumpkin or radish. Is that okay?"
I put two hundred grams of chicken on the cutting board and carefully ready my fork.
I have to at least make the main dish without cutting any corners because of what I told Saber this morning.

page51.text:
"Yes. I am looking forward to it, Shirou."
It's like she can sense my enthusiasm.

page52.text:
...
That has me even more motivated.
I'll poke some holes first with the fork to prepare, and...
